supporting_pages.title: Memorystore for Redis Cluster overview \_|\_ Google Cloud Documentation
evidence_snippets: Memorystore is based on and is compatible with open-source Redis versions 7.2 and earlier and supports a subset of the total Redis command library.
Applications running on Google Cloud can achieve extreme performance by leveraging the highly scalable, available, secure Redis service without the burden of managing complex Redis deployments.
Here is a diagram that illustrates this structure: Memorystore for Redis Cluster instances are composed of a set of shards, each containing a subset of your key space.

supporting_pages.title: "Manage IAM authentication \_|\_ Memorystore for Redis Cluster \_|\_ Google\
evidence_snippets: For your project, use the gcloud compute instances set-service-account command to set a service account and enable the Cloud Platform API scope for your Compute Engine VM. gcloud compute instances set-service-account VM NAME \ --service-account= SERVICE ACCOUNT EMAIL \ --scopes= SCOPE Make the following replacements: VM NAME : the name of your Compute Engine VM SERVICE ACCOUNT EMAIL : the email address of your service account SCOPE : the Cloud Platform API scope for the VM ( cloud-platform ) For example, the following command assigns the my-sa-123@my-project-123.iam.gserviceaccount.com service account to a VM called example-VM and sets the access scope on that VM to the Cloud Platform API: gcloud compute instances set-service-account example-VM \ --service-account=my-sa-123@my-project-123.iam.gserviceaccount.com \ --scopes=cloud-platform For more information about enabling this access scope, see Attach the service account and update the access scope .

Create an instance with IAM authentication To create a Memorystore for Redis Cluster instance that uses IAM authentication, run the create command: gcloud redis clusters create INSTANCE ID --region= REGION ID --network= NETWORK --node-type= NODE TYPE --shard-count= SHARD COUNT --auth-mode=iam-auth Replace the following: INSTANCE ID is the ID of the Memorystore for Redis Cluster instance you're creating.

Troubleshooting error messages with IAM authentication Error message Recommended action Description -WRONGPASS invalid username-password pair or user is disabled Verify the username and access token provided to the Memorystore for Redis Cluster server The username or access token provided is invalid. "default" is the only supported username.
